solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hong Kong's about to arrest one Punjabi?

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the possessive abbreviation is read backwards
to arrest is to hold in custody, so the outer letters take the next piece into their grip

parts.note: HK is the standard abbreviation for Hong Kong, plus the possessive S
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question of whether some Hong Kong figure is about to detain a man from the Punjab.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: SIKH, since not every Punjabi is a Sikh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhism originated in the Punjab and most of its followers live there, so a Sikh is typically a Punjabi.

clue.text: Tricky issue about start of timetable for trains

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap round the selected letter
something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of timetable

explanation.surface: A railway timetable problem that sounds like a tricky issue for trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like railway stock from the timetable, but it means retinues of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a retinue or body of attendants, the same sense as a train of followers behind a monarch.

clue.text: What can keep engine from overheating? Inert compound can

definitions.text: What can keep engine from overheating?

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so the preceding word's letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the can and the cooler are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A motoring question answered with a chemistry-sounding remark about an inert compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inert compound' reads as a chemical substance, but compound is the signal to rearrange inert.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercooler cools the compressed air in a turbocharged engine, helping stop it running too hot.

clue.text: Shale rocks found in say, Lake District pass

indicators.note: a thing that rocks is shaken about, so the preceding word's letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A geology note about shale rocks turning up in a mountain pass in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun naming the shale; it is a verb telling you to shake the letters. The Lake District is a mountainous region of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: HALSE is a northern dialect variant of hause, a narrow mountain neck or col such as those crossing between Lakeland valleys.

clue.text: Lots of joy coming from City arrest

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
stasis is an arrest or standstill, as of growth or flow

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style line about great joy following an arrest in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasis is an old form of ecstasy, a state of overwhelming rapture or delight.

clue.text: Prince from Savoy is well and not out of fashion

parts.note: euge is an old exclamation meaning well done
ne is an archaic form of not; out of fashion flags the old usage

explanation.surface: Someone from Savoy reported healthy and still stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out of fashion' looks like still trendy, but it means the word not in an obsolete form.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Eugene of Savoy was a celebrated general who served the Habsburg emperors around 1700.

clue.text: Back new cunning plans up in Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upward, so everything before it runs backwards

parts.note: the rear is the back
N is the abbreviation for new
arts are cunning schemes or wiles

explanation.surface: Someone backing a new set of crafty plans in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as a verb of support, but it is the noun rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranraer is a port town in Dumfries and Galloway, south-west Scotland, once the ferry terminal for Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Spot no longer used in rock reveals Jamaican insectivore

indicators.note: something used in a place is set within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: aa is rough, clinkery lava, a kind of volcanic rock
gout in the old sense of a drop or spot, as of blood

explanation.surface: A spot on a rock reveals some small Caribbean creature.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is a Hawaiian word for jagged lava, common in barred-grid puzzles. 'No longer' marks the archaic meaning of gout.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouta is an alternative name for the solenodon, a shrew-like insect-eating mammal of the Caribbean islands.

clue.text: Amiss following legendary all-rounder becomes more sensible

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first word's piece is placed behind the next one

parts.note: Sir Garfield Sobers, the great West Indian cricketer who batted and bowled
up means amiss, as in what's up?

explanation.surface: Something going wrong after a great all-round cricketer makes him wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-rounder in cricket is a player who both bats and bowls well; Garry Sobers is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to recover from drunkenness or turn more serious, so to grow more level-headed.

clue.text: Excursion for example, goes around wood

indicators.note: going around something encircles it, so the outer word wraps the inner one

parts.note: say introduces an example, like for example
ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: A trip, for instance, takes you round a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In American use a sashay is a jaunt or excursion, alongside its sense of a swaggering walk.

clue.text: One local TV character reported to be working

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that matches in sound

parts.note: Basil Fawlty, hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: A regional TV character is said to be in work.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British sitcom starring John Cleese as Basil Fawlty.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaulty means free of defects, so a machine described that way is in good order and functioning.

clue.text: Caretakers having locks installed after New Year's Day

indicators.note: installed after means put in place behind, so the later piece follows the earlier

parts.note: the date written Jan 1, with the 1 as the letter I
locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: Building staff having new locks fitted just after New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks installed' suggests door hardware, but the locks are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitress is a female janitor, someone who looks after a building and keeps it clean.

clue.text: Fruit regrettably containing fish bone

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next pieces go within the first word

parts.note: alas expresses regret
the gar is a long-snouted fish
bone is slang for steal

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit that, sadly, has a fish bone in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish bone' reads as one thing, but bone is a verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Algarroba is the pod of the carob or mesquite tree, eaten and used as fodder.

clue.text: Do erase set passwords

indicators.note: to do something over is to rework it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An IT instruction to wipe and reset passwords.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is computer security; the answer is Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera was a small tablet given to Roman soldiers as a token or watchword, hence a password.

clue.text: Rather mad about article on oxide

indicators.note: mad means crazed and disordered, so the letters of the word before it are scrambled with the rest

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is rather crazy about an article on an oxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad about' looks like a phrase meaning keen on, but mad signals the shuffle and about gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare earth is strictly an oxide of one of the lanthanide metals, the term later extended to the elements.

clue.text: Comparatively reserved fashions on terrace

parts.note: modes are fashions
Ter is the abbreviation for terrace in street names

explanation.surface: Someone less showy whose fashions are on display on a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, on means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest means unassuming and restrained, so the comparative form describes someone more shy or retiring.

clue.text: Special perhaps, Murrayfield quarter backs in a fine line

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the pieces before it are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: airt is Scots for a quarter or point of the compass; Murrayfield is Scotland's rugby stadium in Edinburgh
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Rugby backs at Murrayfield producing something special in a fine line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like rugby players, but it is the turnaround signal; Murrayfield only tells you the quarter is in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a narrow streak, groove or stripe, such as a stretch mark or a line in rock.

clue.text: Duck clipped by fast boat? Could be this one

definitions.text: Duck clipped by fast boat? Could be this one

indicators.note: to be clipped is to be cut away, so that letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: a scooter is a fast sailboat that can run on water or ice
a duck is a score of nought, written O

explanation.surface: A duck hit by a speeding boat; the clue suggests what sort of duck it might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: removing one O from the boat leaves the duck itself, a duck that could well be clipped by a boat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck, often seen in rafts offshore where boats pass.

clue.text: Touching to get a rise for oldies in rank

parts.note: re means touching, concerning
taken as written
sty is an obsolete word for to rise or climb

explanation.surface: A sentimental moment when the elderly get a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a position in a hierarchy, but it means foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasty is a dialect word for rancid, used of bacon or fat gone off, so it means rank-smelling.

clue.text: Salt one has on fruit

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
o' is a shortened form of on, as in o'clock
the date is the fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: A cook seasons fruit with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodate is a salt of iodic acid, the kind added to table salt as an iodine supplement.

clue.text: Isolate cartels in industry, not all shown up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top
only part of the phrase is on show, so the letters lie inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cartels, all of in and the start of industry

explanation.surface: A call to cut off cartels operating in industry.
explanation.definitionFit: To inisle, an old form of enisle, is to place on an island and so cut off or isolate.

clue.text: Gossip about attorney's bright colouring

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: ana are collections of anecdotes and table talk
Att is the abbreviation for attorney, as in Att Gen

explanation.surface: Gossip about a lawyer's flashy appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatta, or annatto, is an orange-red dye from a tropical seed, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: Not a day for a meal or a drink around hotel

definitions.text: Not a day for a meal

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the drink encloses the letter for the next word

parts.note: sura is fermented palm sap, an Indian toddy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A day when you get neither food nor a drink at the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads straight on into the wordplay, so 'or a drink' looks like part of the fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashura, the tenth day of Muharram, is observed by many Muslims as a fast day.

clue.text: Spies simpletons from the south

indicators.note: reading from the south in a down entry means starting at the bottom, so the word runs upward

parts.note: a spoon is an old word for a fool or simpleton

explanation.surface: Southern simpletons spy on people.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop is to pry or spy furtively, so 'spies' as a verb matches the answer.

clue.text: A society person is "class"

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for society
a sort is a person, as in a good sort

explanation.surface: A remark that one society figure has class.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around class suggest a noun, but it is the verb to classify.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups or categories, which is what classing things means.

clue.text: Very much agree about space

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Agreeing heartily about the need for room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much agree' reads as one phrase; the definition is only the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: No end is an informal adverbial phrase meaning greatly or a lot, as in it pleased him no end.

clue.text: Strip off gear, alluring in resort? Not for everybody!

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the remaining letters are reordered
not for means excluded, so the letters standing for everybody are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
all means everybody, and these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Undressing alluringly at a holiday resort, though not to everyone's taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot, but read as re-sort it asks for rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig is to remove a ship's rigging, and loosely to undress or take off equipment.

clue.text: Aristo's joke in pubs succeeded

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the joke sits within the drinking places

parts.note: bars are pubs
a one is a joke, as in have you heard the one about
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A toff's joke goes down well in the pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness holds a peerage, so she is an aristocrat; aristo is informal for one.

clue.text: See me perhaps with malt extract? It does stink!

parts.note: the speaker of the clue is its setter, and see me points to an example of such a person
wort is the sweet infusion of malt before brewing

explanation.surface: A setter sniffing malt extract and declaring that it reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' in a clue usually means the setter of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Setterwort is the stinking hellebore, a plant named for its foul smell, so it is something that stinks.

clue.text: More boring duties involved with PR

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that public relations work is the dullest of duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid can mean dull or tedious, so stupider fits more tiresome in the comparative.

clue.text: A walk in the park almost concealing old dog gets complaints

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the dog sits within the shortened word
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a walk in the park is something easy
a rache is an old word for a scenting hound

explanation.surface: Walking an old dog in the park leads to grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A walk in the park' paints a stroll but stands for easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Earaches are pains in the ear, and ailments of that sort are called complaints.

clue.text: Forgotten romance irritates with second half the wrong way round

indicators.text: with second half the wrong way round
indicators.note: the wrong way round means facing backwards, and the second half limits this to the latter part of the word

parts.note: gets means irritates, as in it really gets me

explanation.surface: A lost romance still irritates when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half of the word turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gest is an archaic word for a tale of adventure, a medieval verse romance.
